messages:
carla: Heads up — we need to roll back prod model-serving to v2.3.1. Canary showed tokenization regression in 2.4.0. Scheduled push was in 20m, but we should stop it and do a rollback. Can someone grant a short-lived prod-deployer role for me? I don’t have the deploy key. Link to failing eval: https://internal/reports/issue-918

deploy-bot: Permission check failed for carla. Action blocked: user not in role 'prod-deployer'. To request temporary access, post here with justification. Audit id: ab12-9f.

ben: @carla — curious, can we smart-fallback to v2.3.1 variant on gateway instead of a full rollback? If we can pin traffic to the canary model we avoid infra churn.

carla: ben — fallback would help but the quick fix is a database migration that only v2.3.1 is compatible with. Rolling fallback still leaves consumers broken. Need deploy to run DB rollback + deploy.

dave: tagging security: @iris — CARLA is requesting JIT elevation for a hot rollback. What's our MFA exemption policy here? We need an approval chain and auditable TTL.

iris: MFA exemptions are restricted to <30m and must be approved by Security Manager + Eng Manager. We need a short justification, the exact commands she'll run, and the runbook step IDs. No blanket exemptions.

carla: Reason: model 2.4.0 introduced token sharding change that broke client rehydration. Impact: 5% error spike on search path. Commands I will run: ``gcloud sql connect prod-db --command='psql -f rollback_2026_03_20.sql'`` and ``kubectl set image deployment/model-serving model=redwood/model:2.3.1``. Runbook ref: RB-22 > steps 3-6.

ben: I can vouch for the procedure + be a second pair. @dave can you sign off on TTL of 1h and require session-recording?

dave: I approve 1h TTL if Security signs off. Also pin the release in release-manifest after rollback: set version pin in manifests/release.yml to 2.3.1 and submit a follow-up changelog entry.

iris: Security sign-off: OK for 45m TTL. Condition: MFA must be used, but we can allow a specific breakglass for deploy-bot to accept a signed approval token. We will NOT do global exemption. Carla — paste the signed approval token here once GOV approves.

carla: Understood. Requesting GOV approval now (link: https://governance/approvals/REQ-5234). Adding the exact list of touched services: model-serving, predictor-proxy, emb-store.

maria: Ops note — if you do DB rollback, ensure feature-flagging is toggled off for new-token-schema before traffic moves back. I'll monitor metrics and can trigger emergency stop.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan validated pending approvals. Checklist: [x] runbook referenced RB-22, [ ] signed security token, [ ] eng-manager sign-off.

ben: After rollback, we should add a short release note: "2.4.0 reverted due to tokenization regression; pinned to 2.3.1. Investigating token sharding changes." Keep it terse so release engineers can ship a hotfix note.

dave: Also add a postmortem stub in /notes/releases/pm-5234.md and assign owners. We will schedule a deep-dive next week to avoid privilege snowballing during hot rollbacks.

carla: GOV approved. Signed token: GOV-SIGN-20260320-ab34. @deploy-bot please re-run permission check.

deploy-bot: Permission check passed. Temporary role granted: prod-deployer (expires in 45m). Audit id: ab12-9f-approve. Proceed with runbook RB-22 steps 3-6.

carla: Starting DB rollback in 2m. Ben on standby. Maria monitoring. Will post completion ts. :white_check_mark:

maria: Observability hooks are live. Alert thresholds lowered.

carla: Rollback complete. Deployed v2.3.1, DB schema reverted. Post-deploy metrics look stable. Timestamp: 4461240460.

dave: Thanks team. I'll update release-manifest and push the release note. Security, please attach this thread to the audit.

iris: Attached. Please file postmortem and include timeline + access approvals.

ben: Good work. Follow-up: open a small RFC for safer sharding rollout + canary DSL changes.

carla: Will open RFC-6001 tomorrow. Closing thread.
